title: The Educated Barbarian: Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 8)
summary: NH begins Musashi's Wind Book, using its critique of other schools to argue against dogmatism and marketing in fitness. He applies 'do not cut strongly or weakly, just cut' to lifting tempo, advocating intent to complete the rep over obsessing about speed, and discusses facing fears and seeing naturally.
claims: Know other training styles to understand your own; though he trains purely for aesthetics he follows strongman, powerlifting, arm wrestling and sumo to avoid an echo chamber and dogmatism
In fitness most marketed products are worthless because hard work and consistency cannot be sold; buyers are mostly beginners or people avoiding hard work
You cannot pay your way to a good body with coaching, programs or diets
A teacher who trains only movement without insisting on strengthening the mind leaves an unfinished product with skill but no spirit
Criticize ideas, not names or brands; feuds just breed drama and hurt intellectual discussion
Gurus saying only certain lifts or one rep range work are dogmatic; such rigidity usually comes from tradition or a marketing identity, not from being best
What matters is not the equipment or movement but what you do with it; do not be limited by preconceived properties of tools
Hold firm stances on a few defining values, but nuancing beliefs over time is adapting, not flip-flopping
An open spirit is like a wide stance that keeps you balanced; a proud narrow stance gets knocked over by the first thing
Lift with the intent of finishing the rep rather than fixating on fast or slow; go fast when fast is best and slow when slow is best
Focusing on speed can degrade technique and cause injury, while overly slow tempos kill momentum and strength without real extra benefit
The stretch reflex at the bottom of a lift puts more stress on the muscle than extra time spent slowing the eccentric
Exploding as fast as possible out of a squat can shoot the bar out of position and compromise the rest of the set; push with might but control the energy
Strategy is intelligence: understanding a situation and getting the best out of it
Fears and insecurities exist only because you give them life; chase them off your path and make them obey your will
Seeing naturally (wide awareness without staring) matters little in lifting but helps in sports, martial arts and situational awareness
